properties.name: Any level of the design can be analysed on its own, and a narrowed answer says what it left out
properties.statement: A person or team responsible for one part of a design must be able to point the detectors at that part and be answered about it — "is my subsystem coherent, what is it owed" — without reading the whole program. Anthony, 2026-07-25, from the satellite case: an organisation building a satellite capability has a space segment, a ground/user segment and a control segment; his team owns the satellite, and more specifically inter-satellite laser communications. He must understand the system of systems, but day to day he needs his own part. Two properties are inseparable from the first. A narrowed answer must NAME WHAT IT WITHHELD — findings elsewhere in the design, and findings that belong to no part in particular — because a team shown only its own corner will conclude the program is healthy, which is the silent-drop failure req:no-silent-fallback forbids, one level up from a truncated read. And narrowing must never become the tool deciding what a team is allowed to worry about: a program-level finding that touches their work still reaches them, marked as the program's rather than theirs. Deliberately silent on WHERE the levels live: a subtree of one graph and a design of its own are both answers to this, and that is the architecture question recorded as dec:nested-graphs.
